encounters.cc: Worsening swelling and pain in right foot with non-healing ulcer near the arch.

lines: Worsening swelling and pain in right foot with non-healing ulcer near the arch.
He denies any specific injury but notes that the foot started feeling "puffy" and became more uncomfortable, especially while walking.
He also noticed a small ulcer near the arch that has not healed despite daily dressing changes.

On examination, the foot appears warm, erythematous, and mildly deformed at the midfoot, with decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick over the dorsum and sole.
There is no tenderness to palpation, and distal pulses are palpable.
An x-ray of the foot reveals marked disorganization of the tarsometatarsal joints, with bony fragmentation and joint subluxation.

encounters.cc: Decreased urine output and malaise on day 5 of hospitalization for complicated urinary tract infection.

lines: Decreased urine output and malaise on day 5 of hospitalization for complicated urinary tract infection.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Charcot neuroarthropathy of the right midfoot diagnosed six months prior, and recurrent complicated urinary tract infections who is currently hospitalized.
He was admitted for treatment of a complicated urinary tract infection caused by a Gram-negative bacillus and started on intravenous antibiotics with initial improvement.
On day 5 of hospitalization, he develops malaise and decreased urine output.

lines: Acute onset severe mid-thoracic back pain with high fever, bilateral leg weakness, and urinary retention.
The patient, with poorly controlled diabetes, Charcot neuroarthropathy, and recurrent necrotizing infections, presents with a 3-day history of severe mid-thoracic back pain and fever.
He describes the pain as constant, sharp, and exacerbated by movement.
He also reports mild leg weakness and difficulty urinating.
